name: Clay-Style 3D (Digital and 3D Aesthetics; supplemental design reference, not a named style in the source collection).
visualIdentity: Clay-Style 3D uses rounded forms, restrained handmade surface detail, matte materials, broad lights, and credible contact shadows, with limited colors. It is a digital 3D surface treatment, distinct from physical clay stop-motion. Source data does not specify camera language, lens, or texture detail beyond these cues.
suitableUses: Explicitly listed fits: soft 3D, organic illustration, and material-transformation scenes; interactive campaign heroes with a meaningful impact-and-growth metaphor; stylized scenes whose assets support contact, compression, and surface coverage. Inferred: single-character or product mascot shots, which the source recommends running without hybrids. Multi-character worlds suit a diorama hybrid. Topics needing strict scientific accuracy are unspecified.
limitations: Output must be described as clay-like 3D unless physical clay was filmed. Deformation must stay restrained: no continuous melting, liquid-like flow, or constant wobble, and no uniform spring presets. Glossy or PBR-realistic props conflict with the matte look in hybrid sets. Elastic XPBD does not produce plastic clay, fluid, tearing, or origami behavior, and a simulated appearance is not validated physics.
palette: The palette is an optional suggestion, not supplied colors: background #F2E9DA, foreground #3E4A46, accent_1 #93AD9E, accent_2 #C7917B. Task-provided or approved colors override it and must not be recolored. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background contrast is 7.675, meeting the 4.5 normal-text target. Both accents fail body-text contrast (3.833 and 3.416) and are decorative only. Verify on composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Motion should convey weight and slight elasticity with coherent easing, while preserving deliberate cuts and reading holds. Deformation is reserved for impacts or reactions, and apparent volume should remain constant. The impact-and-growth pattern uses a triggered drop, contact squash, and surface growth from the impact point. Gaze tracking, miniature parallax, camera orbit, chapter transitions, and storytelling are optional and only if assets support them. Video derives all state from composition time; live pointer or scroll input applies only to interactive delivery.
audio: Audio is unspecified in the style data and is a per-task suggestion. Background music, voiceover, vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence should be chosen from the topic, audience, and motion. A restrained sound accent may suit a triggered impact. Speech must stay intelligible and must not compete with narration. The source assigns no fixed genre, tempo, or mandatory audio layer.
assetRequirements: Explicitly required: rounded meshes, matte materials, and broad lighting built in Blender, with controlled deformation and keyframes. The impact pattern needs a modeled or flat-authored orb and receiving surface, plus growth material and accents. Gaze tracking needs suitable eye layers or a rig. Parallax needs layered or 3D assets with crop margins. Orbit needs complete geometry or sufficient turntable views. Fonts and assets must load before rendering. Source-provided asset names are unspecified beyond these examples.
combinations: Clay-Style 3D alone suits single-character or product mascot shots. Suggested hybrids: style-079 for diorama environment staging with matching matte materials and palette, and style-106 for squash-and-stretch timing that preserves volume. Keep depth of field off the main character and avoid mismatched miniature scales. Hybrids stay in Blender, so describe the result as clay-like 3D.
productionApproach: Explicitly, Blender with its bundled bpy module and Cycles or EEVEE acts as both style_renderer and motion_engine, with one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the default composition and export pipeline; Remotion is a fallback only under its documented condition, with the reason recorded. Stateful XPBD simulation should be cached and evaluated from seekable time. chroma-js validates colors. Before delivery, check key frames, direct seeks, audio synchronization, and loop seams. The render commands in the source are suggestions, not verified tooling.
